title: EXCHANGE - the gajin rates, Table 46
audit_comment: OA round twenty-five (capture pp. 76-77): the gajin and rates of exchange prose and the Table 46 exchange grid

banner.title: GAJIN AND RATES OF EXCHANGE AND TABLE 46, printed capture pp. 76-77 - the OA exchange round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture alone for this range (the settling authority): the first Mistral-OCR capture session is unavailable above p. 33, so the cross-capture agreement check is impossible. No contested cells detected within the single source: the T46 grid pins as nine currency rows x 4 cols - the real value as a fen-based absolute (every printed multi-value cell agrees in fen: the silver 10 fen or 2 yuan, the electrum 100 fen or 20 yuan or 1 tael, the gold 200 fen or 40 yuan or 2 tael, the platinum 1000 fen or 200 yuan or 10 tael or 1 ch'ien), the exchange rate as per-row lo-hi bounds in the row's own unit, the market-value rows pinned as the -99 sentinel with a market flag; the row order pins as the 0-8 code: fen, yuan, tael, ch'ien, copper piece, silver piece, electrum piece, gold piece, platinum piece. The prose street rates and the T46 standard rates differ AS PRINTED - the yuan 'also equal to one copper piece' beside the T46 five-copper real value, the tael 4-14 sp (2d6-2) street fetch beside the T46 2-12 sp - both pinned as printed, the prose as the export street rate, the table as the standard doctrine. OCR normalization: the silver rate prints '(1d6 - 7)' and reads as 1d6+7 fen (spanning 8-13), pinned as the dgySilverFenDieOffset const. The Equipping the Character prose with Table 47 (capture pp. 77-84) is deliberately left for the next round
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 88 closed, 147 open - the Gajin and Rates of Exchange and Table 46 boxes flip (census 560 -> 561); NEXT - R639: the Equipping the Character prose with Table 47 (Basic Equipment and Supplies Cost), capture pp. 77-84, the eight cost lists, prefix dgz (verify free), audit "R639 OA equipment audit", include after rules/oaexch.h

consts.name: dgyT46RowCount
consts.comment: Table 46 (capture p. 77): nine currency exchange rows

consts.name: dgyProseFenCp
consts.comment: exchange prose (capture p. 77): one fen is equal to one copper piece - the export equality, agreeing with the T46 fen row real value

consts.name: dgyProseYuanCp
consts.comment: exchange prose (capture p. 77): a yuan is also equal to one copper piece when taken out - the export street rate, printed beside the T46 five-copper real value

consts.name: dgyProseTaelSpLo
consts.comment: exchange prose (capture p. 77): a tael generally fetches 4-14 silver pieces abroad

consts.name: dgyProseTaelSpHi
consts.comment: the upper bound of the tael street fetch in silver pieces (capture p. 77)

consts.name: dgyTaelSpDieSub
consts.comment: exchange prose (capture p. 77): the tael street fetch rolls as 2d6-2 silver pieces

consts.name: dgyProseGoldTaelLo
consts.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): gold prices typically range from 2-7 tael per gold piece when the coins are sold in Kara-Tur

consts.name: dgyProseGoldTaelHi
consts.comment: the upper bound of the gold-piece sale price in tael (capture p. 76)

consts.name: dgySilverFenDieOffset
consts.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): the silver-piece rate 8-13 fen rolls as 1d6+7 - the capture prints '(1d6 - 7)', a dash OCR read (1d6+7 spans 8-13)

bools.name: dgyGajinExchangeNeed
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): a campaign with gajin contact sooner or later has money crossing both ways, and the different coinages force the rates of exchange to be figured

bools.name: dgyMoneylendersExchange
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): along established caravan routes and in major trading ports moneylenders do business in exchanging the two coin types

bools.name: dgyChaoWorthlessOutside
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): the ch'ao is worthless except as an oddity outside of Kara-Tur - and even in some areas of Kara-Tur

bools.name: dgyChaoConvertAdvice
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): before traveling to gajin lands the character is well-advised to convert his ch'ao to something more substantial

bools.name: dgyGoldNotAccepted
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): gold coins are not accepted currency for purchases in Kara-Tur - they can only be sold, because they are gold, at the going price of gold

bools.name: dgyGoldMarketFactors
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): the gold price moves on the amount of gold on the market, the purity (gold coins generally not too pure in content), and the amount sold at once - a large sale floods the market and drives the price down

bools.name: dgySilverForeignUndesired
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): the foreign silver coins are somewhat smaller and of poorer quality than those found in Kara-Tur, and being foreign are not desired by merchants

bools.name: dgyCopperMoreStandard
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 76): copper pieces are somewhat more standard - characters can normally get one fen for every two copper pieces

bools.name: dgyExportSmuggling
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 77): lands with established currency keep their coins within their own lands - minted coinage leaving the country is bad for the economy, and exporting coins is smuggling, a criminal offense

bools.name: dgyKtCoinsAbroad
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 77): Kara-Tur coins smuggled out are more readily accepted abroad, other lands lacking a strong currency system

bools.name: dgyCoinSpeculation
bools.comment: gajin prose (capture p. 77): it is possible for characters to gain or lose money (buying power) by speculating in coins - the motivation of the exchange doctrine

bools.name: dgyRealValueDoctrine
bools.comment: the T46 notes (capture p. 77): Real Value is the absolute value of the coin exchanged, figured as if the two currencies were absolutely identical and exchanged at perfectly equal rates

bools.name: dgyExchangeValueDoctrine
bools.comment: the T46 notes (capture p. 77): Exchange Value is the normal rate of exchange expected from merchants and moneylenders, normally given as a die range allowing less or more than the real value

bools.name: dgyMarketPriceDoctrine
bools.comment: the T46 notes (capture p. 77): Market Price of Metal marks a coin with no equivalent in the other land and not accepted as normal currency - the character has to make a deal for the amount he receives
